record.context_brief: Systematic treatment of multi-loop thermal sum-integrals
record.original_question: Can one develop a systematic, preferably computer-algebraic, method for evaluating the multi-loop thermal sum-integrals that arise in perturbative finite-temperature QCD and related finite-temperature field theories, instead of continuing to solve the needed master sum-integrals one case at a time? Such a method would need to work in the presence of discretized Matsubara frequencies and the additional temperature scale, reuse more of the analytic machinery that is successful at zero temperature than integration-by-parts relations alone, and provide a reusable way to separate ultraviolet and infrared divergent pieces so that higher-order perturbative computations can be streamlined.

evidence.quote: the problem of evaluating the resulting set of master sum-integrals still presents a formidable challenge.
the few sum-integrals that have been computed beyond the 2-loop level have been solved on a case-by-case basis

let us express our hope that a further generalization of the techniques presented here and possibly an automatization of the subtraction procedure will lead towards a computer-algebraic treatment of multi-loop sum-integrals, in order to greatly streamline higher-order perturbative computations in finite-temperature field theories.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic, preferably computer-algebraic, method for evaluating multi-loop thermal sum-integrals of the form
\[
\sumint_{P_1,\dots,P_L} f(P_1,\dots,P_L),\qquad \sumint_P \equiv T\sum_{p_0\in 2\pi T\,\mathbb{Z}\,\text{or}\,(2\mathbb{Z}+1)\pi T}\int\!\frac{d^{d}\mathbf p}{(2\pi)^d},
\]
that arise in perturbative finite-temperature quantum field theory (in particular hot QCD), where each loop momentum carries a discrete bosonic or fermionic Matsubara frequency $p_0$ and a continuous spatial momentum $\mathbf p$ in $d=3-2\epsilon$ dimensions, and the temperature $T$ provides an additional scale relative to vacuum integrals.

The method should:

1. Apply uniformly to entire classes of master sum-integrals (vacuum and with external Matsubara/spatial momenta) at three loops and beyond, rather than addressing them case by case.

2. Beyond integration-by-parts (IBP) identities and a Laporta-type reduction adapted to the broken Lorentz symmetry of the thermal setting, incorporate further analytic machinery known to be effective at zero temperature (e.g., differential equations, Mellin–Barnes representations, dimensional shift relations, hypergeometric/symbolic summation techniques) in a way that respects the discreteness of $p_0$.

3. Provide a reusable, ideally automated, prescription for separating ultraviolet and infrared divergent contributions of each sum-integral, so that the divergent parts are matched against effective-theory (e.g., dimensionally reduced) counterparts and the finite parts are isolated for numerical or analytic evaluation.

Question: Can such a systematic, automatable framework be constructed, in a form that streamlines higher-order perturbative computations at finite temperature?
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: IBP/Laporta-type reductions adapted to Matsubara sums, tensor reduction via dimensional shifts, and partial automation (e.g., "Automated computation meets hot QCD", PoS LL2012; recent 3-loop dimensional reduction work, 2024-2025) have enabled new higher-order thermal QCD results. However, no fully general computer-algebraic framework with automated UV/IR subtraction for all multi-loop master sum-integrals exists; master sum-integrals beyond two loops are still tackled in part case by case. The problem is therefore partially solved and remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Automated computation meets hot QCD (PoS LL2012)
status_evidence.snippet: IBP relations on Matsubara summands used systematically with a Laporta-type reduction for thermal sum-integrals.
status_evidence.claim: IBP-based automation for thermal sum-integrals has been developed and applied to higher-order finite-temperature QCD computations.

status_evidence.title: A new method for taming tensor sum-integrals
status_evidence.snippet: Tensor reduction by dimensionality shifts generalized to finite temperature for three-loop vacuum sum-integrals.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of zero-temperature techniques (dimension-shift tensor reduction) have been extended to thermal sum-integrals.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions in dimensional reduction up to three loops
status_evidence.snippet: Recent three-loop dimensional reduction calculation in hot QCD-like theories.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order thermal computations continue, indicating ongoing but still incomplete automation.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances in perturbative QCD at high density
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews progress and remaining challenges in evaluating multi-loop sum-integrals at finite T and mu.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-loop thermal sum-integral evaluation is still an active, only partially automated, research front.
